body:
Re-scoped by the main session: the constant-engagement half is done - 2D Adaptive is the HSM spiral (53ddc9f, ed393a1, 2e678dd, d352e37), load ~15 % D, 0 breaks past 5°, proved arcs, measured per path by adaptive_hsm's hsm_report. What remains is the trochoidal half: channels and bands too narrow/long for the spiral (the channel fixture, the user's Outside band from #13 - 'Offset rings cut this pocket instead') should get trochoidal loops at constant engagement instead of rings.

claimed: main session (agent: trochoidal channels) · 2026-11-07T01:35Z · worktree on 37b9bbd · plan: a trochoid planner along the channel's medial line for narrow regions, used where the HSM spiral refuses; engagement/kink/air measured like the spiral.

Cause: where the HSM spiral cannot plan an area (a long thin channel or band refused by the planning budget, #13; the 22x60 channel and island fixtures past the hop/rest budget), `pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes` hands it straight to Offset rings, which in a channel just under 2 D run at full slotting engagement.

Plan: a trochoidal fallback between the two (spiral -> trochoid -> rings, each named in the op notes).
1. Medial line of the centre area: offset it inward by most of its half-width until it is a thin strip (open channel: averaged from the strip's two sides) or a thin annulus (closed band: midway between its two loops); the loop radius is the least clearance along it, less a margin, so the tool centre never leaves the centre area.
2. Trochoidal loops along it (Otkur & Lazoglu 2007; Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009): front arcs of radius rho advancing by s per loop, s chosen on the planner's stock against the same load target as the spiral. The verifier's crossing law (Feed-Feed crossings at a shared depth block the post) rules out the textbook circular trochoid, whose loops cross each other; the front arcs are therefore trimmed short of +-90 deg so consecutive arcs never cross, and the air return rides the existing microlift return.
3. Entry by the existing helix/plunge law at the line's start, a rounded wall lap last.
4. Measured like the spiral (load % D, breaks > 5 deg, air) with report rows for the channel and band fixtures.
Anything not proven inside this pass stays gated off rather than shipped active.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Progress (staged in a worktree, uncommitted, gated off; nothing changes behaviour yet):

Landed:
- `adaptive/medial.rs`: the medial line of a channel-like centre area. The area is offset inward by 0.92 of its half-width. A thin strip is averaged from its two sides and trimmed where its clearance drops under 0.985 c (the corner branches). A thin annulus gives a closed line midway between its two loops. Anything else (the island pocket) is refused by name.
- `adaptive/trochoid.rs`: the trochoid's front arcs, each aimed along its centres' advance, plus a step chooser on the planner's stock (the spiral's ladder, against the spiral's bound). The verifier's crossing law blocks the post on Feed-Feed crossings at a shared depth, and full trochoid loops cross each other. So only the front arcs are cut, trimmed to +-(90 deg - s/rho - 0.03), and they never cross.
- Readings on the planner stock (D10, 14.6% load): channel 22x60 had rho 5.70, s 0.513, 75 loops, load 14.2% D. The 14 mm band had rho 1.90, s 0.103, 2575 loops, load 15.6% D. That band step is impractically short.

Still to do before it can be wired in (spiral -> trochoid -> rings in `pocket_hsm`):
1. The air return between front arcs as a microlift `Return` (`lift_link`), and its proof against the crossing law.
2. Arc starts that land on cleared stock (one descent per level).
3. The rounded wall lap, plus the entry helix at the line start.
4. The band's step: a larger rho/s pair, or loops that are not circular.
5. adaptive_hsm report rows and the end-to-end test (load, breaks > 5 deg, verify clean, centre area).

Tests: `medial::tests::a_channel_medial_line_runs_down_its_middle`, `a_band_medial_line_closes_round_it_and_an_island_pocket_is_refused`, `trochoid::tests::trochoid_front_arcs_hold_the_load_never_cross_and_stay_in_the_center_area`, `trochoid_on_the_users_band_holds_the_load_and_never_crosses`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Groundwork landed in 5f87518 (Refs #5, switched off; medial line + front arcs at the load target, 4 unit tests). Still owed before it is switched on: (1) lifted microlift returns between front arcs, proved against the crossing law; (2) arc starts on cleared stock (one descent per level); (3) a rounded final wall lap + helix entry; (4) a practical step for the 14 mm band (now 0.103 mm × 2575 loops); (5) adaptive_hsm report rows + an end-to-end test; (6) flip shoulder/adaptive_band's refusal expectation. Claim stays with the main session; round 2 next.

Round 2 (staged in worktree agent-af493aee8d4f2d538 on 5f87518, uncommitted). Everything is wired; the trochoid is held off by one law.

**Wired:** `pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes` now runs spiral -> trochoid -> rings for the planar pocket, and each fallback is named in the notes. The 3-D ladder passes `false` for now.
- `pocket_troch.rs` adds the entry (`EntryRoom` at the medial line's start, with the helix seed a radius behind it) and holds the plan to the crossing, budget and rest laws.
- `adaptive/troch_plan.rs` does the rest:
  - an opening spiral from the helix out to the loop circle
  - the front arcs, each reached by a microlift return (lifted, never crossing another, off the helix orbit, lowest lift that clears)
  - a tangent blend onto nested wall laps whose corner radius steps down from the half-width to 0.25 r; corner scallop named.

**Readings with the landing law relaxed** (channel 22x60, release, full-resolution yardstick):
- load 15.4% D (bound 16.1%), 0 breaks past 5 deg, 0 slot, verifier clean, no crossing
- rest 11.97 mm2 (corner scallop named), 3716 moves (254 arcs)
- 58 arcs at rho 5.70 and s 0.659
- cut 2862 mm, floor air 1159 mm, lift 1202 mm (x0.82)
- 0 retract hops, **but 118 descents**

**What keeps it off:** every ramp lands on an arc start that is already in cut, with the crescent and the 0.33 mm wall strip inside the measuring rim. So each loop counts as a descent into stock. The plan now refuses that by name ("lands on a loop start already in cut"), and the channel stays on Offset rings with the reason in its notes. The 14 mm band is refused by name too: no room to open out, and 2575 loops would be over `LOOP_CAP` 600. Both are tracked in #47.

**Tests:**
- `troch_tests::the_channel_trochoid_lifts_every_return_never_crosses_and_holds_the_load`
- `troch_tests::a_landing_on_a_loop_start_in_cut_is_refused_by_name`
- `adaptive_hsm::the_channel_names_the_trochoid_fallback_before_the_rings` (heavy lane: 80 s in debug)

**Gates:**
- `-Tier quick` green (31 motion suites + area_open)
- `adaptive_hsm` debug + `hsm_report_full_resolution` release ok; the load law holds and the channel row still reads GAP (rings)
- app `shoulder_adaptive`, `golden_cl` and `operations` ok
- clippy `-D warnings` clean

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Round 2 in f796e52 (Refs #5): the trochoid fallback is wired (spiral → trochoid → rings, named) and holds the load law on the 22×60 channel (15.4 % D, 0 breaks, clean verify), but its returns land on arc starts already in cut (118 descents vs the one-descent law), so it is refused by name and the channel stays on rings. The concrete blocker is #47 (an air lead into each arc that crosses no floor feed). Claim released; priority P1 → P2: the constant-engagement spiral the user hits is in place, and the remaining trochoid work is an improvement for narrow channels, gated on #47.
blocked on #47 (legal landings for the trochoid's returns).
